items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bookkeeping.

the principle that only items large enough to affect a decision need separate disclosure
the book in which transactions are first recorded with their debit and credit entries
the rule that the business is treated as separate from its owners in the records
items.s: Bookkeeping: the routine recording of business transactions in the books of account. The other options describe Business entity concept, Materiality, Journal.

items.q: Matching concept is best described as
o: the comparison of two figures from the accounts to judge performance
the difference between the two sides of an account
the conventional account drawn with a left and a right side
the rule that expenses are set against the income of the same period
items.s: Matching concept: the rule that expenses are set against the income of the same period. The other options describe Ratios, T account, Balance.

the method that writes off an equal amount of cost each year
items.s: Straight line depreciation: the method that writes off an equal amount of cost each year. The other options describe Suspense account, Contra entry, Bank reconciliation statement.

items.q: The statement “an entry that transfers an amount between two accounts on the same side, as in cash to bank” describes which of the following?

Bank reconciliation statement
Contra entry
Stakeholder
items.s: Contra entry is an entry that transfers an amount between two accounts on the same side, as in cash to bank.

items.q: All of the following belong to Bank reconciliation EXCEPT
o: Straight line depreciation
Uncredited deposit
Unpresented cheque
Bank reconciliation statement
items.s: Every other option belongs to Bank reconciliation. “Straight line depreciation” belongs to Measuring profit, not Bank reconciliation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Stakeholder?

a person or group with an interest in the reports of a business, such as owners or lenders
the collection of all accounts of a business
an arrangement allowing a creditor to collect varying amounts from the account
items.s: Stakeholder: a person or group with an interest in the reports of a business, such as owners or lenders. The other options describe Direct debit, Error of commission, Ledger.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Imprest system.

the owner's residual interest in the assets after deducting liabilities
the rule that the business is treated as separate from its owners in the records
the conventional account drawn with a left and a right side
items.s: Imprest system: the arrangement in which petty cash is restored to a fixed float at the end of each period. The other options describe T account, Business entity concept, Capital.

items.q: Petty cash book is best described as

current assets divided by current liabilities, showing short-term liquidity
a cheque issued by the business but not yet presented at the bank
the book used to record small cash payments under the imprest system
items.s: Petty cash book: the book used to record small cash payments under the imprest system. The other options describe Current ratio, Going concern concept, Unpresented cheque.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Credit?

an entry made in the wrong class of account altogether
the right-hand side of an account, used for increases in liabilities, capital and income
the routine recording of business transactions in the books of account
items.s: Credit: the right-hand side of an account, used for increases in liabilities, capital and income. The other options describe Bookkeeping, Matching concept, Error of principle.

items.q: The statement “the comparison of two figures from the accounts to judge performance” describes which of the following?

Going concern concept

an instruction to the bank to pay a fixed sum at regular intervals
the rule that expenses are set against the income of the same period
the duty of management to account to the owners for the resources entrusted to them
items.s: Reducing balance depreciation: the method that charges a fixed percentage of the remaining book value each year. The other options describe Matching concept, Stewardship, Standing order.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Suspense account.

the temporary account opened to hold a difference in the trial balance until it is found
the routine recording of business transactions in the books of account
the assumption that the business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future
items.s: Suspense account: the temporary account opened to hold a difference in the trial balance until it is found. The other options describe Going concern concept, Stewardship, Bookkeeping.

items.q: Sales day book is best described as

an error in which the debit and credit entries of a transaction are reversed
an arrangement allowing a creditor to collect varying amounts from the account
items.s: Sales day book: the book that lists credit sales to customers. The other options describe Direct debit, Error of omission, Complete reversal of entries.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Gross profit?

the right-hand side of an account, used for increases in liabilities, capital and income
the difference between net sales and the cost of goods sold
the branch that records past transactions and reports them to owners and other outsiders

the principle that only items large enough to affect a decision need separate disclosure

the left-hand side of an account, used for increases in assets and expenses
money paid in by the business but not yet credited by the bank
the branch that records past transactions and reports them to owners and other outsiders

an entry made to the correct class of account but to the wrong personal account
the branch that prepares information for internal decision making by managers

Current ratio
Error of commission

the process of identifying, recording, classifying and summarising transactions and interpreting the results

the assumption that the business will continue to operate for the foreseeable future
the convention of providing for losses as soon as they are foreseen but not anticipating profit
